football_evidence.question: Can UNLV contain Wyoming’s explosive runs?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward Wyoming, and its own breakdown accounts for about 0.0 of the 2.2 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When UNLV has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): UNLV’s offense has allowed a sack on 7.2% of its dropbacks, and Wyoming’s defense sacks the quarterback on 6.3% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).
When Wyoming has the ball (the run game against the run defense): Wyoming’s offense averages 6.4 yards per carry, and UNLV’s defense allows 5.8 yards per carry (FBS average 5.0).

When Wyoming has the ball (big plays on the ground): Wyoming’s offense turns 9.6% of its runs into explosive gains, and UNLV’s defense gives up explosive gains on 8.7% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).
When UNLV has the ball (the red zone): UNLV’s offense succeeds on 38.3% of its red-zone plays, and Wyoming’s defense allows success on 35.4% of opponent red-zone plays (FBS average 43.5%).
contradicting: When UNLV has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): UNLV’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 14.2% of its runs, and Wyoming’s defense stops 11.7% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.5%).

When Wyoming has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Wyoming’s offense has allowed a sack on 8.5% of its dropbacks, and UNLV’s defense sacks the quarterback on 5.0% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).
When UNLV has the ball (third down): UNLV’s offense converts 50.6% of its third downs, and Wyoming’s defense allows opponents to convert 39.0% of their third downs (FBS average 39.6%).
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put UNLV’s receivers No. 45 nationally and Wyoming’s No. 119.
quarterbacks: Jackson Arnold has completed 127 of 214 passes (59.3%) for 1,650 yards, 7.7 yards per attempt, 12 touchdowns and 4 interceptions in eight games for UNLV, and has been sacked on 17 of 231 dropbacks.
Tyler Hughes has completed 108 of 172 passes (62.8%) for 1,143 yards, 6.6 yards per attempt, 5 touchdowns and 7 interceptions in eight games for Wyoming, and has been sacked on 15 of 187 dropbacks.
